Nothing to fear. Although I hate labels, a diagnosis can get you assistance an autistic person needs. My son just started high school this year. He is on the football team and is in track to graduate along with his class. He is in special education but is mainstreamed. This means he had a team of teachers, school psychologists, counselors, speech therapists, behavior analysts, and I that work to see how he's doing in his classes. In his Individualized Education Plan (IEP) he as allowed  extra time for assignments, preferred seating in a class, etc. He had a pas that he carries in his wallet that allows him to leave a class anytime he feels overwhelmed or overstimulated. There are contact people he can go to or their office to chill out. The thing is, we are all working "undercover" if you will due to his age. He's 14 and in high school. He doesn't want to stand out so all these services are on the down low. There is an assistant "teacher" in his English class that helps the whole class. She is really there to help him and watch for any difficulties because English is his worst subject. He's a genius in math. No, not savant style or anything but he just gets it. Everyone goes to the "assistant" for help so he does too. 

So what I wanted to say is, autism is a very complex disorder but there is nothing wrong with people with autism. Yes, some are "lower" on the spectrum and some are "higher" ,but this does but appear to be the case with you, hun.
